title: Snapshot failures found during R CMD Check
description:
Hello, We've been running `R CMD check` for packages for our package registry manager PRISM ([Home | PRISM](https://prism.dev.a2-ai.cloud/)) and noticed that `connectcreds` is failing during tests. We found the root cause to be new versions of `httr2` as the snapshot test passes when using  `httr2 1.1.0` an older version . We've seen similar `httr2` related test failures across several other packages.
The full error output:
```
checking tests Running testthat.R
  Running the tests in tests/testthat.R failed.
  Last 13 lines of output:
    - [1] "Key key"
    -
    - $headers$Accept
    - [1] "application/json"
    -
    - attr(,"redact")
    + <httr2_headers>
    + Authorization: <REDACTED>
    + Accept: application/json
    and 4 more ...
    [ FAIL 1 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 9 ]
    Error: ! Test failures.
    Execution halted
```
Here is the failing test:
```
test_that("token exchange requests to Connect look correct", {
  local_mocked_connect_responses(function(req) {
    # Snapshot relevant fields of the outgoing request.
    expect_snapshot(
      list(url = req$url, headers = req$headers, body = req$body$data)
    )
    response_json(body = list(access_token = "token"))
  })
  expect_equal(connect_viewer_token()$access_token, "token")
})
```

Expected Snapshot:
```
$headers
$headers$Authorization
[1] "Key key"

$headers$Accept
[1] "application/json"

attr(,"redact")
[1] "Authorization"
```

Snapshot when tested:
```
$headers
<httr2_headers>
Authorization: <REDACTED>
Accept: application/json
```

Happy to provide any more details or clarity if needed.

title: connectcreds::connect_viewer_token() fails when current shiny session is a namespaced session (ie session_proxy)
description:
When using shiny::ns() in modules, connectcreds::connect_viewer_token() fails with:

Error:
! `session` must be a Shiny session object, not a <session_proxy> object.

The issue stems from:
- https://github.com/posit-dev/connectcreds/blob/main/R/viewer-based-credentials.R#L197-L206


- You can of course bypass this by rewriting your shiny module to pass the parent session into the module so that you have reference to the real shiny session object.
   - However, this does no good when using the odbc::databricks() driver because there is no way (that I can see) to pass any of the connectcreds::connect_viewer_token() arguments into the odbc package for it to use.

It's basically this error:
```
x = shiny::MockShinySession$new()$makeScope("test")
if (!missing(x) && inherits(x, "ShinySession")) {
    return(invisible(x))
}
rlang:::stop_input_type(
    x,
    "a Shiny session object"
)
```

title: Add a helper to return a AzureToken object to enable use of `Microsoft365R` and `AzureGraph` packages
description:
For Posit Connect customers who want to use the [Microsoft Graph OAuth Integration](https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/msgraph/), their only option currently is to use the MS Graph API endpoint directly, which is painful. We have an [example here](https://docs.posit.co/connect/cookbook/content/integrations/msgraph/viewer/r/).

To enable easier access to SharePoint and other Microsoft 365 services from Connect `connectcreds` could create a helper function which would return a [Azure OAuth 2.0 token classe](https://github.com/Azure/AzureAuth/blob/master/R/AzureToken.R), which can then be passed in to many `Microsoft365R` and `AzureGraph` R package functions/methods as the `token` argument. This object is based on the [httr Token2.0 class](https://httr.r-lib.org/reference/oauth2.0_token.html).

This workflow would allow for customers to do (just an example, implementation may be different):

```
azure_token <- connectcreds::connect_viewer_token(output="AzureToken")

Microsoft365R::list_sharepoint_sites(token = azure_token)
```

title: RSTUDIO_PRODUCT is deprecated; support POSIT_PRODUCT
description:
This calls for helper(s) to determine which environment is being used. For example:
- `connectcreds::is_running_on_connect()`
- `connectcreds::is_running_on_workbench()`

or something similar to encapsulate the check.

Need to check both `RSTUDIO_PRODUCT` and `POSIT_PRODUCT` since older versions of connect and workbench will not have the latter set, but when it is set, they will be the same value. RSTUDIO_PRODUCT has not yet been removed, only deprecated for now.

Once merged, ensure that any documentation examples in our products use these helpers for the latest version of this utility. Add fallback note if not on version that includes these helpers.
